title: Asking about more musicians: Barth, Shannon, Newrock, Christians, Mendelson, Majada
summary: Allen reads through names of local musicians and Brunies says what he knows of each: their playing, age, whether read by music, and neighbourhood ties.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: There are a couple of other trumpet players. I was going to ask some names I don't know about. George Barth. Do you remember? Oh, Barth.
Yeah, he used to play a piece of two sometimes.
He played? Yeah. Was he a fairly old man? Is he older than you? No, he's about my age. About your age.
I think so. I don't know about him.

He used to go on the love of Paul Young Abner. And he used to play with fish sometimes, you know. Sometimes when I couldn't make it, why, he went and played with fish. You remember Harry Shannon. Harry Shannon, yeah. He was an umpore player. He was an umpore player.
What do you mean by that? He wasn't very good? He wasn't good at all.
Oh, we know Harry. He was raised. Yeah, Harry Shannon. You're on Little Jackson. He played a, well, a straight. Yeah, just a straight. Like in church. Yeah. Good church.
Yeah, I know Freddie. Newrock, is it? Freddie Newrock. Yeah, he played in all these big brass bands. Seems like it. But all about music. He played by music. He couldn't fake a note.

Another name I have here is Pete Dietrich. Do you remember that? Pete Dietrich. Pete, it looks like Dietrich. No, I don't remember. Is that a white man? Yes, I think so. And Doc looks like Berriesen. B-E-H. Orange? Orange? No, B-E. B-E-H-R-E-A-S-O-N. Barenzy? Barenzy? Barenzy? Barenzy? Maybe that's it. Barenzy? No, I don't know. Doc? I don't know. Yeah. No, I don't know yet. Those are some of the names I was going to ask you about. And what about the Christian boys? Do you remember them? All of them. Yeah. All Frank Christian, Charlie Christian, Johnny Christian.
Emil. Emil, he's still around. He is. He's still playing bass with them, isn't he? Yes, he plays bass. He still plays his trombone sometimes. Yeah, yeah. Double's on.

No, I don't know. Double. Down the corner. Brookhaven. I know all of Brookhaven. Can any of them down? No, I don't. That's probably it. That's it there. Might be not from Brookhaven. Brookhaven, yeah. Yeah. Might be there. They used to have a big brass band, too. I don't know if they played with them. Richard, do you remember old man Mendelson that used to play piano from the neighborhood? His son's playing with the Dukes of Dixieland now. Yeah, Stanley Mendelson. The boy. Mendelson. Huh? Mendelson. Well, his daddy was really more of a good, I mean, a note man. Was he an organist? I think he was. He was an organist. Yeah. I don't think Dick knows him.

He was from the neighborhood originally. I was going to ask about Joe Lala, too. Did he have a band? Yeah, he had a band. He was pretty cool in the right town. And... And... They had two brothers. Yes, Johnny... Johnny and... Johnny.
And the Majada boys. Sala Majada.
Sala Majada. I played with them. One boy plays clarinet. He's living in. He's living in. He's living in.

Johnny, he died not so long ago. And Vincent? And Vincent. Vincent was married to... Vincent don't play. Who was the one who played the clarinet? Johnny. Johnny. He's the one who married to... Teresa Gates. Gates, I mean. Living on Phillips Street. He married everyone from across the river. No, but his first wife was Teresa Gates. Gates. My mother's cousin. Living on Phillips Street.
